record.original_question: For a periodic channel flow initially close to a monotone plane-parallel profile and containing a kink in one initial vorticity level set, show that the kink persists under Euler evolution and does not smooth out over time.

evidence.quote: Problem 23. Show that the “kink” does not disappear as the fluid evolves in time.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the two-dimensional incompressible Euler equations on a periodic channel $\Omega = \mathbb{T} \times [0,1]$ (with $\mathbb{T} = \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$), written in vorticity form
$$\partial_t \omega + u\cdot\nabla \omega = 0, \qquad u = \nabla^\perp \psi, \qquad -\Delta \psi = \omega,$$
with impermeable boundary conditions $u\cdot n = 0$ on $\partial\Omega$. Let $U(y)$ be a smooth plane-parallel shear profile whose vorticity $\Omega(y) = -U'(y)$ is strictly monotone in $y\in[0,1]$, so that the level sets of $\Omega$ are the horizontal lines $\{y = \text{const}\}$.

Let $\omega_0$ be a smooth initial vorticity on $\Omega$ that is a small perturbation of $\Omega(y)$ in a suitable topology, and suppose that exactly one level set $\Gamma_0 = \{\omega_0 = c_0\}$ of $\omega_0$ is a simple closed curve (in the channel) which is smooth away from a single point $p_0$ where it has a corner — a "kink" — i.e. the curve $\Gamma_0$ has two distinct one-sided tangent directions at $p_0$, while all other level sets of $\omega_0$ are smooth.

Let $\omega(t,\cdot)$ be the solution of the Euler equation with initial data $\omega_0$, and let $\Gamma_t = \{\omega(t,\cdot) = c_0\}$ be the corresponding level set transported by the flow.

Prove that the kink persists for all time: there exists a point $p_t \in \Gamma_t$ (depending continuously on $t$) at which $\Gamma_t$ has a corner singularity, and in particular the level set $\Gamma_t$ does not become $C^1$-smooth at any time $t>0$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears in a 2022 compendium of open problems in geometric hydrodynamics (most recent version updated January 2023). No subsequent published resolution of the persistence-of-kinks problem was located in a web search, and no preprint claiming a solution was found. The problem is therefore listed as open.

status_evidence.title: Geometric Hydrodynamics in Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: A collection of open problems in geometric hydrodynamics; includes problems on long-time behaviour of Euler flows and singular vorticity.
status_evidence.claim: The kink-persistence question is stated as an open problem in this 2022/2023 compendium and no later resolution was located.
